seoTitle: Shark vs Dyson Cordless Vacuum UK: Which to Buy in 2026
title: Shark vs Dyson cordless vacuum UK: which to buy in 2026
description: Shark vs Dyson cordless vacuums compared on weight, pet hair, battery, warranty and price, with today's best UK deals on each.
intro:
**For most homes in November 2026, the best buy is the Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute at £349.99 at Argos, its lowest tracked price, if you want light and easy; pick a Shark if you have long-haired pets or want a self-emptying dock and a longer warranty.** Both brands clean about as well as each other. The real differences are weight, pet hair handling, extras and price.

Prices on this page were checked at Argos, John Lewis, AO, Very and the Dyson and Shark websites on 14 November 2026.

deals.name: Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute Cordless Vacuum
deals.note: About 2.2kg, with a laser that lights up dust and a screen that counts what it picks up. £349.99 is PriceSpy's lowest and matches last Black Friday; John Lewis is the same. Best for flats and smaller homes.

deals.note: Comes with a dock that empties the bin for you, plus an anti hair wrap brush roll for pets. Shark's own site is the same price. Argos and Shark quote different 'was' prices (£549.99 and £569.99), so don't read much into the saving.

deals.name: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute Cordless Vacuum
deals.note: More suction and a bigger bin than the V12, for bigger homes and carpets. AO and Very are £479 too, and that's the lowest PriceSpy has recorded.

deals.name: Dyson V8 Cyclone Cordless Vacuum (2026)
deals.note: The cheapest Dyson stick we found, with no sensors or screen. The V8 Advanced hit £199 last Black Friday, so this could drop further.

body:
## Shark vs Dyson: the quick answer

- **Choose Dyson** if weight matters most (stairs, a flat, arthritis in your hands) or you like gadgets such as the dust-revealing laser and the particle-count screen.
- **Choose Shark** if you have pets or long hair in the house, you'd like a dock that empties the bin for you, or you want the longest warranty.
- **On cleaning power**, reviewers generally call it close to a draw. TechRadar put the Shark Stratos and Dyson V15 level on performance, and Shark tends to do slightly better with larger bits of debris.

## Weight and handling

This is where Dyson clearly wins. The V12 Detect Slim weighs about 2.2kg and the V15 about 3.1kg. Shark's cordless models are heavier: the PowerDetect Clean & Empty is about 3.7kg and the Stratos about 4.1kg. You notice that extra kilo when you're doing the ceiling corners or carrying it upstairs.

Shark claws some back with handling. Its wand bends in the middle, so you can get under beds and sofas without kneeling. Its models also have an on/off button, while some older Dysons need you to hold a trigger the whole time.

## Pet hair and long hair

Shark's anti hair wrap brush roll is its best-known feature, and it's the one owners praise most. Hair is cut and pulled off the roller as you go, so you don't have to cut tangles out with scissors. Dyson's newer floor heads also resist tangles, and some reviewers rate its mini grooming tools higher, but if long hair is your main problem, Shark is the safer bet.

## Battery and bin

Both brands claim up to about 60 to 70 minutes, but those figures are for the lowest power setting with a non-motorised tool. On full power on carpet, expect closer to 10 to 20 minutes from either. Both brands' batteries can be removed and replaced, which matters if you want the vacuum to last five years or more.

Shark's bins are usually bigger (around 0.9L on the Stratos, against 0.77L on the V15). The Clean & Empty models also come with a 2L base that empties the bin automatically, which is great for allergy sufferers who don't want to empty it by hand.

## Warranty

- **Dyson:** two years parts and labour on cordless vacuums.
- **Shark:** five years on the vacuum if you register it, but only two years on the battery. Register within 28 days or the cover drops.

## Price: what to pay

Shark is usually cheaper and discounted more often, but check the price history before trusting a Shark 'deal'. On 14 November, Argos and Shark's own site listed the Stratos IZ400UKT at about £450, while price trackers show it normally sells for around £200 to £265 elsewhere. Don't pay £450 for one.

Good prices to aim for this month:

- **Dyson V12 Detect Slim Absolute:** £349 or less (it's there now)
- **Dyson V15 Detect Absolute:** £480 or less (it's there now)
- **Dyson V8:** around £199 to £240
- **Shark Stratos:** under £265
- **Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty:** under £370

Skip the Dyson V11 for now: at £429 at AO, it costs more than the better V12 Detect Slim.

For more prices, see our [Dyson Black Friday deals 2026](/guides/dyson-black-friday-deals-2026/) and [Shark Black Friday deals 2026](/guides/shark-black-friday-deals-2026/) guides, or [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/).

### Is Shark as good as Dyson?

For cleaning, mostly yes. Reviewers find suction very close between similar-priced models. Dyson is lighter and has more gadgets; Shark is better on hair tangles and better value.

### Which is better for pet hair, Shark or Dyson?

Shark, by a small margin, thanks to its anti hair wrap brush roll. Dyson's newer heads have closed the gap, so either will cope with a short-haired dog or cat.

### Which lasts longer?

Both use replaceable batteries. Shark's five-year registered warranty is longer than Dyson's two years, though the Shark battery itself is only covered for two.

### Should I wait for Black Friday?

Not for the Dyson V12 Detect Slim or V15 Detect: both are already at their lowest tracked prices. For a Dyson V8 or a Shark Stratos, it's worth waiting until 27 November to see if prices drop.

### Is a Shark vacuum cheaper on Amazon?

Often. Check Amazon's price against Argos before buying, especially for the Stratos, where shop prices vary by around £200.
